**Finding submitted: deviation (critical).**

**What the document does:** Article XII "INDEMNITY" (p0128–p0129) is entirely one-way — Licensee indemnifies Licensor for our exercise of the license, the conduct of our business, and any breach by us. There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement. Article XIII (p0130) goes further and states that "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED ... IN ANY INFRINGEMENT," and the warranty disclaimer strips non-infringement. So the Vendor affirmatively disclaims the exact exposure the playbook requires it to cover.

**Why deviation, not fallback:** This is the rule's walk-away fact pattern — no Vendor IP indemnity at all combined with a one-way Customer indemnity for the Vendor's own technology. Under this Agreement we license and deploy the Vendor's platform but bear 100% of third-party infringement risk, against a Licensor cap of one-half of amounts paid.

**Redline (validated ok:true), three minimal ops:**
1. Narrowed our indemnity trigger (i) from "exercise of any license or other rights" to Licensee-provided content, data or materials.
2. Narrowed triggers (ii)/(iii) from "conduct of Licensee's business" and any breach of the Agreement down to "Licensee's breach of applicable law."
3. Inserted a Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation, Licensor's breach of law, Licensor-caused unauthorized access to our data, and Licensor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation and consent-to-settle mechanics.

One drafting point worth flagging: I added an express carve-out stating the Licensor indemnity applies notwithstanding Article XIII. Without it, the existing infringement disclaimer and the one-half-of-fees cap would swallow the new indemnity and leave us with illusory protection. The comment offers the fallback (customary IP exclusions for our modifications/combinations/specifications, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies, and a 3× annual fees super-cap) as a negotiated landing zone.
